title: Tom Preston-Werner and the Semantic Versioning Spec
explainer: The MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH convention this lesson covers, and the whole idea that a version number is a promise other tools can rely on, was formalized as a written specification by GitHub cofounder Tom Preston-Werner in the late 2000s. He wrote it because, without a shared convention, every package maintainer was making up their own rules for what counted as a "breaking" release — npm, Cargo, and most modern package managers now build their automatic-upgrade behavior directly on top of his spec.

title: Stuart Feldman and the Invention of Make (1976)
explainer: Make — and the tab-indented recipe syntax this lesson warns you about — was written by Stuart Feldman at Bell Labs in the spring of 1976, by his own account after a colleague lost a morning's work to a stale, un-rebuilt executable. Feldman's core idea, comparing file modification timestamps to rebuild only what's out of date, is exactly the dependency-graph behavior this lesson demonstrates, and it earned him the ACM Software System Award in 2003 for a tool still shipped on every Unix-like system half a century later.
